feature: Dimension-scoped WHERE filters a type-scan by a spine dimension value

scenarios.name: scan filters pg_node by a dimension value
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — no applicable feature folder (TAP-native: Entity dimension scoping)

scenarios.name: a dotted path into dimensions names ONE flat key and matches the dotted dimension
scenarios.note: `tap.playground` is a real dotted TAP dimension key and every node in this fixture carries it, so a correct lowering returns all four. Before req-grid-traversal-lang-envelope-paths-9 the dot spelling lowered each step separately — `dimensions #> ARRAY['tap','playground']`, a NESTED path no conformant flat `dimensions` value can hold — and under 3VL the missing path was NULL, so the query returned a clean, alarmless ZERO rows. Four-vs-zero is the assertion; do not reshape this onto the undotted `zone` key, which cannot tell the two lowerings apart.
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — no applicable feature folder (TAP-native: dimensions is a TAP spine field with no TCK analogue)

scenarios.name: the bracket spelling of the same dotted key is the same lookup
scenarios.note: The equivalence half of envelope-paths-9: `n.dimensions.tap.playground` and `n.dimensions["tap.playground"]` MUST be the same lookup. Its SQL snapshot is byte-identical to dimensions__dot_run_key.sql.txt apart from the two spellings sharing one plan — `cmp` the two files when either changes. The bracket spelling was always correct; it is here as the fixed point the dotted spelling had to be moved onto.
scenarios.inspired_by: opencypher TCK — no applicable feature folder (TAP-native: dimensions is a TAP spine field with no TCK analogue)

scenarios.name: a dotted dimension key that no node carries returns an empty envelope, not a silent one
scenarios.note: The non-matching companion. The defect's whole danger was that a WRONG lowering also returns zero rows, so an empty expected envelope proves nothing on its own — the SQL snapshot carrying the literal `'nope'` against the SAME flat-key path as the matching scenario is what makes this empty non-vacuous.
